@gridsheet/preact-core.name: GridSheet Preact
@gridsheet/preact-core.shortDescription: Spreadsheet component with formulas and multi-sheet support for Preact.
limitations: Requires @gridsheet/functions when using the spellbook helpers.
Lists dayjs as an additional runtime dependency in upstream docs.
SSR behavior has not been independently verified for PreactHub.

sections.Introduction: GridSheet provides an Excel-like spreadsheet UI for Preact through the dedicated `@gridsheet/preact-core` renderer. It ships a native Preact peer dependency and exposes `GridSheet`, spellbook helpers and formula-aware cell editing.
sections.Preact configuration: Install `preact ^10.26.6` as a peer dependency. Import components from `@gridsheet/preact-core` and optional spellbook utilities from `@gridsheet/preact-core/spellbook` when formulas are required.
sections.SSR notes: Upstream documentation focuses on client-side spreadsheet interaction. PreactHub has not verified a supported SSR path; treat server rendering as unknown until you validate DOM measurement and formula evaluation in your target environment.
sections.Islands notes: Spreadsheet widgets are usually mounted as self-contained interactive islands because they depend on pointer, keyboard and scroll interactions.
sections.Known limitations: Formula support depends on `@gridsheet/functions`. Large workbooks can be heavy for island hydration, and accessibility for grid navigation should be validated against your product requirements.
sections.Alternatives: For tabular data without spreadsheet semantics, see [TanStack Table](/libraries/tanstack-table).

@clean-jsdoc-theme/rang.name: Clean JSDoc Theme Rang
@clean-jsdoc-theme/rang.shortDescription: Preact component library, MDX map and island registry for Clean JSDoc Theme v5.
limitations: Designed for Clean JSDoc Theme v5 page shells rather than general-purpose app UI.
Reuse outside the dwar/rang architecture requires reviewing island registry contracts.

sections.Introduction: `@clean-jsdoc-theme/rang` is the native Preact surface for Clean JSDoc Theme v5. It provides SSR chrome (`Layout`, `Header`, `Footer`), interactive documentation islands (`Sidebar`, `ThemeToggle`, `CtrlK`, code tabs and copy helpers) and the `defaultMdxComponents` map used by the theme renderer.
sections.Preact configuration: Import chrome, islands and MDX helpers directly from `@clean-jsdoc-theme/rang`. Pair the package with `@clean-jsdoc-theme/utils` island names through the exported `ISLAND_REGISTRY` when wiring hydration entry points.
sections.SSR notes: Chrome components are SSR-only while islands render meaningful initial HTML and hydrate for keyboard handling, theme persistence, clipboard actions and navigation affordances.
sections.Islands notes: Each island listed in `ISLAND_REGISTRY` is bundled as its own ESM chunk by the theme pipeline. Scope hydration roots per island name (`sidebar`, `theme-toggle`, `cmdk`, and others) to avoid duplicate client controllers.
sections.Known limitations: The package is tightly coupled to Clean JSDoc Theme infrastructure. Using individual islands in unrelated Preact apps may require replicating locale and theme providers exported alongside the components.
sections.Alternatives: For general documentation sites outside Clean JSDoc Theme, compare with [PreactPress](/libraries/preactpress) or your static-site generator of choice.

@lynx-js/react-signals.name: Lynx React Signals
@lynx-js/react-signals.shortDescription: Thread-aware Preact Signals integration for ReactLynx applications.
limitations: Targets ReactLynx runtimes, not standard browser-only Preact applications.
ReactLynx currently requires reading signal values through `.value` rather than passing Signal objects directly in JSX.

sections.Introduction: `@lynx-js/react-signals` exposes Preact Signals APIs (`signal`, `useSignal`) adapted for ReactLynx's multi-thread rendering model. Signals stay reactive on the background thread while first-screen rendering on the main thread uses static values.
sections.Preact configuration: Use this package only inside ReactLynx projects that already depend on Preact Signals semantics. Import from `@lynx-js/react-signals` instead of `@preact/signals` when building Lynx UI modules.
sections.SSR notes: ReactLynx first-screen rendering uses static signal values on the main thread. Validate hydration and background-thread updates within the Lynx toolchain rather than assuming standard Preact SSR behavior.
sections.Islands notes: Not applicable to conventional Preact island architectures; this adapter is specific to ReactLynx page and component lifecycles.
sections.Known limitations: This is not a drop-in replacement for `@preact/signals` in normal web apps. Follow Lynx documentation for thread constraints and JSX consumption rules.
sections.Alternatives: For browser Preact apps, use [Preact Signals](/libraries/preact-signals).

@formepdf/preact.name: Forme PDF Preact
@formepdf/preact.shortDescription: Native Preact adapter for the Forme declarative PDF component model.
limitations: Advanced PDF features should be checked against Forme component docs before production use.
@formepdf/core is optional when serializing to JSON for the hosted API instead of local rendering.

sections.Introduction: `@formepdf/preact` mirrors the Forme React component set with a Preact-native JSX runtime. It avoids pulling React or `preact/compat` into PDF generation pipelines while keeping the same document serialization API as `@formepdf/react`.
sections.Preact configuration: Set `jsxImportSource` to `preact` in TypeScript or add `/** @jsxImportSource preact */` at the top of files that render PDF trees. Requires `preact ^10.19.0` as a peer dependency.
sections.Example:
```tsx
import { Document, Page, Text, View, renderDocument } from "@formepdf/preact";

const pdf = await renderDocument(
  <Document>
    <Page size="Letter" margin={36}>
      <Text style={{ fontSize: 24, fontWeight: "bold" }}>Invoice #001</Text>
      <View style={{ flexDirection: "row", justifyContent: "space-between" }}>
        <Text>Widget Pro</Text>
        <Text>$49.00</Text>
      </View>
    </Page>
  </Document>,
);
```
sections.SSR notes: PDF trees are rendered programmatically through `renderDocument` and do not require a browser DOM, making the adapter suitable for server-side generation when `@formepdf/core` is installed.
sections.Islands notes: Typical usage is server-side or worker-side document generation rather than client islands. Client previews should treat PDF bytes as output artifacts.
sections.Known limitations: Confirm which chart, form-field and layout primitives you need against the Forme docs. Hosted-API workflows can omit `@formepdf/core` but lose local rendering.
sections.Alternatives: If you already standardize on React compatibility shims, `@formepdf/react` with `preact/compat` remains possible but adds runtime overhead.

@tanstack/charts.name: TanStack Charts
@tanstack/charts.shortDescription: Headless chart definitions with an official Preact adapter export.
limitations: The Preact adapter is imported from the @tanstack/charts/preact subpath rather than a separate npm package.

sections.Introduction: TanStack Charts separates chart definitions from rendering. The official Preact adapter exports a `Chart` component from `@tanstack/charts/preact` that hydrates SVG produced during SSR and delegates interaction to the shared chart runtime.
sections.Preact configuration: Define charts with `defineChart` from `@tanstack/charts` and optional modules such as `@tanstack/charts/tooltip`. Render them through the Preact adapter import path `@tanstack/charts/preact`.
sections.SSR notes: The adapter emits the complete accessible SVG during Preact server rendering and adopts it after mount. Keep definitions, formatters and dimensions deterministic between server and client renders.
sections.Islands notes: Chart widgets are good island candidates because the adapter manages mount, resize and cleanup per host element.
sections.Known limitations: Use the documented subpath import `@tanstack/charts/preact`; there is no separate npm package name for the adapter.
sections.Alternatives: See [uPlot](/libraries/uplot) for a lighter canvas-oriented option or [Chart.js](/libraries/chart-js) for canvas charts via compatibility layers.

praxis-kit.name: Praxis Kit
praxis-kit.shortDescription: Contract-driven component factory with a dedicated Preact adapter subpath.
limitations: Project is young (0.1.x) and classified experimental until broader PreactHub verification.
Structural ARIA and children contracts add runtime diagnostics that should be tuned per environment.

sections.Introduction: Praxis Kit provides `createContractComponent`, a factory for typed, accessibility-aware UI primitives. The Preact adapter lives at `praxis-kit/preact` and shares enforcement, styling and preset logic with the React, Vue, Solid and Svelte adapters.
sections.Preact configuration:
Import the Preact adapter subpath:

```ts
import { createContractComponent } from "praxis-kit/preact";
```

Factory options such as `tag`, `styling`, `enforcement` and `defaults` match the other framework adapters.
sections.SSR notes: Upstream conformance tests include SSR and hydration parity across adapters. Start with `diagnostics: "warn"` during development and tighten enforcement once contracts are stable.
sections.Islands notes: Contract components work well inside islands when enforcement diagnostics are scoped to development builds.
sections.Known limitations: Praxis Kit is early-stage. Review API stability notes in upstream docs before adopting widely, and expect iteration on adapter subpaths.
sections.Alternatives: For hand-written accessible primitives, compare with [Kamod UI](/libraries/kamod-ui) or established design systems listed under UI Components.

@rsbuild/plugin-preact.name: Rsbuild Preact Plugin
@rsbuild/plugin-preact.shortDescription: Official Rsbuild plugin for Preact JSX, compat aliases and Prefresh HMR.
limitations: @rsbuild/plugin-preact v2 requires Rsbuild 2.x; use v1 on Rsbuild 1.x projects.

sections.Introduction: `@rsbuild/plugin-preact` is the official Rsbuild plugin for Preact applications. It wires JSX compilation, optional React compatibility aliases and Prefresh-powered hot module replacement into Rsbuild config.
sections.SSR notes: Rsbuild handles server and client bundles; verify SSR-specific externals and rendering entry points in your deployment target.
sections.Islands notes: Build-tooling only. Island architectures inherit whatever client entries Rsbuild emits.
sections.Known limitations: Match plugin major versions to your Rsbuild release. Custom refresh scopes can be configured through `preactRefreshOptions`.

vitest-browser-preact.name: Vitest Browser Preact
vitest-browser-preact.shortDescription: Browser-context renderer for Preact components in Vitest 4+.
limitations: Requires Vitest 4.0.0 or higher with the browser test runner enabled.

sections.Introduction: `vitest-browser-preact` adds a Preact-aware `render` helper to Vitest's browser mode so component tests run against real browser DOM APIs instead of emulated environments.
sections.Preact configuration: Import `render` from `vitest-browser-preact` inside browser tests, or rely on the injected `page.render` helper when Vitest exposes the browser page object.
sections.SSR notes: Testing utility only; not used in production SSR pipelines.
sections.Islands notes: Useful for verifying island components with real layout, focus and pointer behavior in browser tests.
sections.Known limitations: Requires Vitest 4 browser mode. Wrapper components and custom containers are supported through the render options object.
sections.Alternatives: For jsdom-style unit tests, [Preact Testing Library](/libraries/preact-testing-library) remains the lighter default.

@monza-editor/preact.name: Monza Editor Preact
@monza-editor/preact.shortDescription: Lightweight textarea-based code editor component for Preact.
limitations: Syntax highlighting is supplied by a user-provided highlight function rather than built-in language packs.

sections.Introduction: Monza Editor wraps a textarea with syntax-highlight overlays. The `@monza-editor/preact` package exposes the Preact component while keeping the core editor bundle extremely small.
sections.Preact configuration: Provide a `highlight` function that converts source text into HTML annotated code. Style the editor with monospace `font-family` and optional CSS variables such as `--me-padding`.
sections.SSR notes: The editor relies on textarea selection and overlay synchronization that should be validated if you render initial HTML on the server.
sections.Islands notes: Code editors are commonly mounted as islands to defer highlight logic and keep static pages lean.
sections.Known limitations: Bring-your-own highlighter means you must sanitize or trust highlight output. For full IDE features, heavier editors may be more appropriate.
sections.Alternatives: See [Preact RichTextArea](/libraries/preact-richtextarea) for simpler text areas or evaluate full Monaco integrations separately.

@xstate/store-preact.name: XState Store Preact
@xstate/store-preact.shortDescription: Official Preact bindings for @xstate/store selectors and triggers.

sections.Introduction: `@xstate/store-preact` provides Preact hooks such as `useSelector` for stores created with `@xstate/store`. It complements the core [XState](/libraries/xstate) entry by documenting the dedicated Preact adapter introduced in XState Store v4.
sections.Preact configuration: Import `createStore` from `@xstate/store` and Preact bindings from `@xstate/store-preact`. Framework bindings are no longer exported from `@xstate/store/preact` in v4.
sections.SSR notes: Store reads during render should use snapshot APIs on the server and subscribe on the client. Verify hydration when preloading store state.
sections.Islands notes: Shared stores can back multiple islands if you expose selectors scoped to each widget's concerns.
sections.Known limitations: Requires TypeScript 5.4+ according to upstream XState Store docs. Use full XState when you need statecharts rather than lightweight stores.
sections.Alternatives: Compare with [Preact Signals](/libraries/preact-signals) for fine-grained reactivity or the core [XState](/libraries/xstate) package for state machines.

extension.name: Extension.js
extension.shortDescription: Cross-browser extension framework with first-class Preact support and HMR.
limitations: Targets browser extension runtimes rather than conventional web applications.
Preact is one supported frontend option alongside React, Vue and Svelte templates.

sections.Introduction: Extension.js is a cross-browser extension toolchain with Manifest V3 defaults, store-ready zip builds and hot module replacement for background, content, popup and options scripts. Preact is supported through dedicated templates and refresh shims.
sections.Preact configuration: Scaffold with the Preact template (`npx extension@latest create my-extension`) or add Extension.js to an existing extension repository. The CLI detects Preact and wires refresh support for extension entry points.
sections.Example:
```bash
npx extension@latest create my-preact-extension --template preact
cd my-preact-extension
npm run dev
```
sections.SSR notes: Not applicable. Extension pages run inside browser extension contexts rather than on a hosted SSR server.
sections.Islands notes: Popup and options pages behave like small isolated Preact apps; content scripts should minimize shared state with page DOM.
sections.Known limitations: Validate target browsers (Chrome, Edge, Firefox, Safari) for your manifest features. Extension.js focuses on developer experience rather than acting as a general web app framework.
sections.Alternatives: Also evaluate WXT, Plasmo or CRXJS if you need different extension toolchain trade-offs.

mixed-signals.name: Mixed Signals
mixed-signals.shortDescription: Transport-agnostic RPC and signal reflection built on Preact Signals Core.
limitations: Requires configuring a transport (WebSocket, SSE, postMessage, etc.) and server-side model registration.
Reconnection and authorization semantics depend on your RPC transport implementation.

sections.Introduction: Mixed Signals reflects server-side Preact models and signals—created with `@preact/signals-core`—to connected clients through a lightweight RPC protocol. Client facades stay in sync without manually mirroring every signal update.
sections.Preact configuration: Use `mixed-signals/server` on the host and `mixed-signals/client` inside Preact components. Register models on the server RPC instance before accepting client connections.
sections.SSR notes: Server models run outside typical Preact SSR trees. Render client proxies only after the RPC session is established.
sections.Islands notes: Real-time widgets backed by shared server state are natural island candidates; isolate RPC clients per island root.
sections.Known limitations: Verify transport security, reconnection and cleanup for your deployment. The protocol optimizes deltas but still requires a correctly configured server model registry.
sections.Alternatives: For local-only reactive state, use [Preact Signals](/libraries/preact-signals) without RPC overhead.

@css-hooks/preact.name: CSS Hooks Preact
@css-hooks/preact.shortDescription: CSS-in-JS hooks for conditional inline styles in Preact components.
limitations: Relies on modern CSS variable features; verify browser support for your audience.
SSR and hydration behavior should be validated when styles depend on client-only measurements.

sections.Introduction: CSS Hooks adds conditional styling to native Preact inline styles using CSS variables—covering pseudo-classes, selectors and container queries without runtime style injection. `@css-hooks/preact` is the dedicated Preact adapter.
sections.Preact configuration: Import helpers such as `pipe` and `on` from `@css-hooks/preact` and compose them inside component `style` props.
sections.SSR notes: Inline styles serialize with the Preact element tree. Confirm container-query and pseudo-class hooks behave as expected after hydration.
sections.Islands notes: Hook-based styles work inside islands because they avoid global stylesheets; still scope any shared CSS variables at the island root.
sections.Known limitations: Upstream browser support starts at Chrome 99+, Safari 15.4+ and Firefox 97+. Complex responsive rules should be tested in target browsers.
sections.Alternatives: For utility-first class workflows see [Tailwind CSS](/libraries/tailwind-css) or [Panda CSS](/libraries/panda-css).
